senses.gloss: to go into exile, go away, disappear.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Hosea 10:5">Targ. Hos. X, 5</cite>.—
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Hosea 11:11">Ib. XI, 11</cite> <he>דִּיגְלוֹ</he> those who were exiled.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Amos 5:5">Targ. Am. V, 5</cite> <he>מִיגְלָא יִגְלוּן</he> (some ed. <he>ילפון</he>, corr. acc.); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 56a:19">Ber. 56ᵃ</cite> <he>אִגְלֵי</he> I will leave home; <he>גלא לבי רומאי</he> he emigrated into Roman territory.
<cite ref="Pesachim 49a:17">Pes. 49ᵃ</cite> <he>לא גְלָאִי</he> I should not have emigrated; <he>לא גלאי כדגָלֵי אינשי</he> I did not emigrate (voluntarily) as others do.
Koh. R. to IX, 10 את הוית גָּלֵי וכ׳, v. אֲלַף II.—Part. גָּלֵי, pl. גָּלַיָּא, f. גָּלָן exiles.

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Nahum 2:8">Targ. Nah. II, 8</cite> <he>בגָלַיָּא</he> ed. among the exiles (on foot; ed. Lag. <he>בגִילַּיָּא</he>, v. <cite ref="C00730"><he>גִּילּוּיָא</he></cite>, h. text <he>גֻּלְּתָה</he>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Amos 6:7">Targ. Am. VI, 7</cite> <he>גָּלָן</he> the exiled communities.—
Targ. II Kings XXIII, 6 קברי ג׳ (some ed. גַּלּ׳) the graves of the homeless (h. text בני העם).—Part. pass. גֱּלֵי, גֲּלִי, גְּ׳, גַּלְיָא known, revealed; uncovered.
<cite ref="Daniel 2:19">Dan. II, 19</cite>; <cite ref="Daniel 2:30">30</cite>.

<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 14:8">Targ. O. Ex. XIV, 8</cite> <he>בריש ג׳</he> openly (h. text <he>ביד רמה</he>).
<cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 18:6">Targ. Lev. XVIII, 6</cite> sq.; a. fr.
<cite ref="Gittin 31b:13">Gitt. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>ג׳ לדרעיה</he> he uncovered his arm.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 28a:5">Ab. Zar. 28ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yoma 84a:4">Yoma 84ᵃ</cite> <he>דלא מְגַלִּית</he> that thou wilt not divulge it.
<cite ref="Yoma 84a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>מְגַלִּינָא</he> I shall divulge.
<cite ref="Chullin 113a:6">Ḥull. 113ᵃ</cite> <he>תנא סיפא לגַלּוּיֵי רישא</he> the second clause is stated in order to throw light on the first.

<cite ref="Gittin 34a:13">Gitt. 34ᵃ</cite> <he>גַּלּוּיֵי דעתא</he>, v. <cite ref="C00730"><he>גִּילּוּיָּא</he></cite>. Y. Maasr. V, end, 52ᵃ <he>מן דגַלִּית לך חספא אשכחת מרגניתא</he> (not <he>דגליית</he>) after I removed the potsherd, thou foundest the pearl, i.e. but for my teaching, you would not have found the truth which you now claim as your own discovery; Y. Keth. IX, 33ᵇ bot. (corr. acc.); [in Babli <he>דלאית</he>, v. <cite ref="D00827"><he>דלי</he></cite>].

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Samuel 6:20">Targ. II Sam. VI, 20</cite> <he>דא׳</he> who exposed himself; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 109b:9">Snh. 109ᵇ</cite> <he>אִיגְּלָאִי מלתא</he> the fact became known.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 22b">R. Hash. 22ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>כל מילתא דעבידא לאִיגְּלוּיֵי וכ׳</he> people are not presumed to tell a lie which is likely to be found out.
<cite ref="Sotah 22b:6">Sot. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>מאי דמִגַּלְּיָא מגליא</he> what is visible is visible, i.e. man judges only by what he can ascertain, opp. <cite ref="M01032"><he>מטמרא</he></cite>.—
R. Hash. 21ᵇ whence do we know that alil לישנא דמִיגְּלֵי הוא has the meaning of being clearly visible? Ab. Zar. 30ᵃ איגלי ליה חמרא his wine was found uncovered.
<cite ref="Beitzah 3a">Bets. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>מִגְּלוּ וקיימי</he> remain visible; a. fr.
